fair_value_reason: The revised agents converge at $7.3-7.4 on shared, verified inputs: 2027 adj FCF ~$940M over ~670M shares (~$1.40) at an 18-19% yield gives ~$7.5; 7.0-8.0x on ~$0.94 EPS gives ~$6.6-7.6; and 4.6-4.75x on ~$2.7B EBITDA less ~$7.5B net debt gives ~$7.5-7.9. I found no further share-count, EPS-base or net-debt errors, so ~$7.35 stands. It is ~21% above spot, but the 12-month median is lower (~$6.45) because of the hiking regime, the block overhang and negative momentum.
supervisor_summary: The five revised forecasts are tightly clustered: fair value $7.3-7.4, P(>= $6.08 in 12 months) 0.53-0.57, and thesis break $4.30-4.50. I keep their mean ladder. Both of agent_5's disputed inputs check out. October hike odds are ~31% (Polymarket) and ~35% (CME) after soft August core PCE, not 67%, though December is still ~71%. The 2022-23 hiking-cycle median 12-month return was indeed -7%, but that rests on ~1.5 independent episodes and is not representative of today's depressed starting price. These facts move only the 1-month view (slightly up and narrower, since the Q3 print is probably after Oct 30), so confidence is low and the mean stands.
key_drivers: 2027 adj FCF of ~$930-950M (~$1.40/share) after the CFO-flagged $50-100M each of cash-tax and interest headwind and no repeat of the 2026 working-capital gain. First test: the FY2026 report and 2027 outlook in Feb/Mar 2027

Rate path: the Fed hiked Sep 16 to 3.75-4.00%. October hike odds fell to ~31-35% after soft core PCE (3.0% vs 3.3%), but December is still ~71%. Swaps expire at end-2026 and the $1B 3.375% notes mature Aug 2027 (refi likely ~6%)
State Farm's 133.3M registered, unsold shares (19.72%, $9.00 cost): a block with an ADT buyback is neutral, open-market selling is negative
Subscriber health: RMR -1% y/y, attrition 13.1%, H1 credit-loss provisions +23% and write-offs +31% (10-Q)
Buybacks (~$885M left) shrink the share count ~10% a year at ~$6; the peer anchor (Verisure) has itself de-rated
